rationale: Lurasidone (D2 full antagonist) to aripiprazole (D2/D3 partial agonist). Both drugs have low metabolic risk and low QTc risk — a good lateral switch for patients prioritising a clean metabolic and cardiac profile. Common reasons: food adherence difficulties with lurasidone, cost, or desire for aripiprazole's mood-stabilising augmentation profile. Aripiprazole's partial D2 agonism may cause akathisia, particularly in the first 2–4 weeks, in patients stabilised on full D2 blockade. Cross-taper preferred over direct switch to allow gradual receptor adaptation. Activation and insomnia are also common on aripiprazole initiation. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start aripiprazole 10 mg. Continue lurasidone 80 mg with main meal. Counsel about akathisia risk in first 2 weeks — restlessness, inability to sit still. Propranolol PRN can be prescribed proactively.
Increase aripiprazole to 15 mg (target). Reduce lurasidone to 40 mg. Review akathisia at end of week 1.
Reduce lurasidone to 20 mg. Aripiprazole at steady state. Insomnia may emerge as lurasidone's mild sedation is lost.
Stop lurasidone. Continue aripiprazole 15 mg. Prolactin normalises rapidly — counsel female patients about menstrual restoration.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Lurasidone 80 mg ≈ aripiprazole 15 mg (inferred from DDD equivalence; limited direct data). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
